problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{3}\,k.$

feedback.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=\,i-\,j+2k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\,i+\,j.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,p(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})p(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-\,j+2k)+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+\,j) \\  & =\sqrt{2}(i+k)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}(i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
 $T(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+k).$
